name: drop_in_place
declaration: unsafe fn drop_in_place < T : ? Sized > (to_drop : * mut T)
rules: to_drop must be valid for reads.
to_drop must be valid for writes.
to_drop must be properly aligned, even if T has size zero.
to_drop must be nonnull, even if T has size zero.
The value pointed to by to_drop must be valid for dropping, including upholding any additional invariants required by its type.
While drop_in_place is executing, parts of to_drop may be accessed only through the mutable self references supplied to the Drop::drop methods it invokes.
If T is not Copy, the pointed-to value must not be used after drop_in_place, including assignment that would drop it again; overwriting the data without dropping it is permitted.
Pinned data must not be moved before it is dropped.
Unaligned values must be copied to an aligned location using ptr::read_unaligned before being dropped; for packed structs, the compiler performs this move automatically.
